primary.name: os-taxonomy
primary.used: 数学学科划分 · 节点 · 前置依赖边 · 年龄分层

secondary.name: cn-k12-math-knowledge-graph
secondary.used: 人教版年级 / 册次 / 章节归属

chains.briefZh: 数位、计数、整数的大小结构——一切计算的地基。先把「数是多少」这件事彻底钉死，再谈运算。
chains.briefEn: Place value, counting and the structure of integers — the bedrock every calculation rests on.

chains.briefZh: 加减乘除的**意义**先于**算法**。竖式是熟练度的终点，不是起点。
chains.briefEn: Meaning before algorithm — column methods are the end of fluency, never the start.

chains.briefZh: 从「一个整体的几分之几」到比例与百分数——分数是数的语言第一次抽象化的地方。
chains.briefEn: From parts of a whole to ratio and percentage — where numbers first become abstract.

chains.briefZh: 长度、面积、体积——所有几何的度量学根基，也是把抽象图形锚定到真实世界的第一根绳。
chains.briefEn: Length, area and volume — the metrological root of all geometry.

chains.briefZh: 三角形、圆、多边形与变换——从「看形状」走到「证形状」，几何证明是逻辑推理的第一战场。
chains.briefEn: Triangles, circles, polygons and transformations — from seeing shapes to proving them.

chains.briefZh: 用字母表示未知数，把「平衡」变成可以动手称量的实物——等式是等量代换的语法。
chains.briefEn: Letters for unknowns, balance made physical — equations as the syntax of equivalence.

chains.briefZh: 从坐标到函数——把「变化」本身变成可以描点、可以拟合的对象。
chains.briefEn: From coordinates to functions — making change itself plottable.

chains.briefZh: 收集、整理、读图、判断可能性——从「描述数据」走到「用数据下判断」。
chains.briefEn: Collecting, organising, reading charts and judging likelihood — from describing data to deciding with it.

nodes.descriptionEn: Each object gets exactly one mark — count one, mark one. The first stone of number sense.
nodes.descriptionZh: 每个物品只配一个标记，点一个数一个。数量感的第一块基石。
evidence: Point to or touch each object exactly once while saying number names
Do not skip objects or double-count when counting a set
Recognise an error when someone counts an object twice
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} is counting a pile of grapes, do they touch or point to each one exactly once as they say each number — without skipping any or counting the same one twice?

nodes.descriptionEn: Lay two piles side by side and pair them off to see who has more, fewer, or the same.
nodes.descriptionZh: 两堆东西并排放，用配对的方式判断谁多谁少、多出几个。
evidence: Use one-to-one matching to compare two groups
State which group has more/fewer after counting both
Use the language 'equal to', 'more than', 'less than', 'fewer', 'most', 'least'
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If you put 6 raisins in one hand and 4 in the other and ask {{name}} which hand has more, can they work it out — either by counting or just by looking?

nodes.nameZh: 基准线上的长短与高矮
nodes.descriptionEn: Misaligned starts give misleading lengths. Align the origins first, then compare.
nodes.descriptionZh: 起点没对齐，长短就看错。先对齐起点，再谈比较。
evidence: Stand two children back-to-back and say who is taller/shorter
Directly compare the heights of two towers and describe one as taller
Use 'longer' and 'shorter' to compare two ribbons placed side by side
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} stands next to the kitchen table and the front door, can they tell you which is taller — and whether they themselves are shorter or taller than each one?

nodes.descriptionEn: Break a whole into parts and put it back together — splitting and combining are two views of one number.
nodes.descriptionZh: 把一个整体拆成几份再合回去——分与合是数的两种看法。
evidence: Look at a ten frame showing 7 and say 'five and two more makes seven' without counting every dot
Name the two parts on a domino showing 4 and 2 and say the total is 6
Show 8 as two groups (e.g. 4 and 4, or 5 and 3) and name the parts quickly
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} looks at a domino with 4 dots on one side and 2 on the other, can they quickly say 'four and two make six' without counting every dot?

nodes.descriptionEn: Ten singles bind into one bundle — this is why 14 is one ten and four ones.
nodes.descriptionZh: 满十根捆成一束，为什么 14 是「一捆十加四根」。
evidence: Group 10 single cubes into one rod of 10 and explains why
Explain that 10 ones is the same as 1 ten
Exchange 10 ones for a single tens block
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Can {{name}} explain that ten single objects bundled together make 'one ten' — and that this is why we write 10 with a 1 in the tens place and a 0 in the ones place?

nodes.descriptionEn: The same digit in a different place stands for a completely different amount.
nodes.descriptionZh: 同一个数字站在不同的位上，表示的大小完全不同。
evidence: Use knowledge that 34 = 30 + 4 to help add 34 + 20 = 54
Solve 'I think of a number, add 10, and get 45. What was my number?'
Apply partitioning to solve a problem in an unfamiliar context
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} is asked 'which number is closest to 50 — 47 or 54?', can they use their number knowledge to answer quickly and explain why?

nodes.descriptionEn: Use place value, not the number of digits, to decide whether 58 or 83 is larger.
nodes.descriptionZh: 用位值而不是「数位个数」来判断 58 与 83 谁大。
evidence: Correctly place > or < between 34 and 43
Order a set of numbers from smallest to largest, including numbers either side of 100 (e.g. 98, 104, 111, 120)
Explain a comparison by referring to the highest place value first — hundreds when comparing across 100 (e.g. 98 < 104 because 104 has 1 hundred), then tens and ones when needed
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If you show {{name}} cards with 104, 98, 120 and 111, can they put them in order from smallest to largest — and use > or < correctly, such as 98 < 104?

nodes.descriptionEn: Can they be shared out two by two with nothing left — from laying out objects to stating the rule.
nodes.descriptionZh: 能不能两个两个正好分完——从摆实物到说规则。
evidence: Identify whether a given number is odd or even
Explain that even numbers can be divided into 2 equal groups
Spot the pattern: even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If you give {{name}} a number like 37 or 84, can they quickly tell you whether it's odd or even — and explain how they know?

nodes.descriptionEn: Put two piles together — how many altogether?
nodes.descriptionZh: 把两堆东西并到一起，一共有多少。
evidence: Model 'putting together' with physical objects and say the total
Act out an 'add to' situation (e.g. 3 children arrive, then 2 more join)
Explain that addition means finding how many altogether
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} has 4 toy cars and a friend brings 3 more, do they understand that adding means combining both groups — and can they tell you there are now 7 cars altogether?

nodes.nameZh: 减法的含义：拿走或分开
nodes.descriptionEn: Take some away from a pile, or split a pile into two parts.
nodes.descriptionZh: 从一堆里拿走一些，或者把一堆分成两部分。
evidence: Model 'taking away' with physical objects and say how many remain
Act out a 'take from' situation (e.g. 5 biscuits, eat 2, how many left?)
Explain that subtraction means finding how many are left
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} has 9 biscuits and eats 3, do they understand that subtracting means taking some away — and can they tell you 6 biscuits are left?

nodes.descriptionEn: Adding the same number several times is what multiplying is.
nodes.descriptionZh: 几个相同的数加起来，就是乘。
evidence: Explain that 3 groups of 2 is the same as 2 + 2 + 2
Use objects to make equal groups and count the total
Recognise an array as showing equal rows
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} needs to count 4 bags with 3 apples in each, can they see that instead of counting all 12 one by one, they could add 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 — or say '4 groups of 3'?

nodes.descriptionEn: Share the same amount among the same number of people — how many each?
nodes.descriptionZh: 把同样的东西分给同样多的人，每人分到几个。
evidence: Share 10 counters (real or on-screen) equally between 2 plates
Group 20 objects into sets of 5 and find there are 4 groups, e.g. by skip counting 5, 10, 15, 20, or alternatively by subtracting 5 repeatedly (20, 15, 10, 5, 0)
Use concrete objects or a drawing to solve 'How many groups of 2 in 8?'
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} has 12 grapes to share equally between 3 friends, can they work out that each friend gets 4 — and explain what they did?

nodes.descriptionEn: The times table grows out of the meaning of multiplication, not out of memory.
nodes.descriptionZh: 九九表不是背出来的，是从乘法的意义里长出来的。
evidence: Quickly answer 5 × 3 = 15 from memory
Quickly answer 20 ÷ 5 = 4 from memory
Recite the 2, 5, and 10 times tables fluently
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Can {{name}} quickly recall times table facts from the 2s, 5s, and 10s — like '5 × 6 = 30' or '20 ÷ 2 = 10' — forwards and backwards?

nodes.descriptionEn: The equals sign is a balanced see-saw, not a 'the answer is here' arrow.
nodes.descriptionZh: 等号是「两边一样重」的跷跷板，不是「答案在这里」。
evidence: Explain that 6 = 6 is true because both sides are the same
Determine that 4 + 1 = 5 + 2 is false
Understand that = does not mean 'the answer comes next' — it means balance
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Does {{name}} understand that '=' means 'the same as', so they can tell you whether '4 + 3 = 8 − 1' is true or false?

nodes.descriptionEn: When it does not divide evenly, what do the leftovers mean?
nodes.descriptionZh: 分不完的时候，剩下的那几个怎么算。
evidence: 52 children go on a trip in minibuses holding 9 each — how many minibuses are needed? (interpret the remainder, including a calculator display such as 5.777… meaning 6 minibuses)
A shop sells packs of 6 pencils for £1.50 each — how much do 5 packs cost?
Represent a two-step problem with an equation using n for the unknown
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} reads 'a school buys 7 boxes of 24 pens and shares them equally between 8 classes', can they work through all the steps and decide sensibly what to do with any remainder?

nodes.descriptionEn: Get a rough value first, then use it to check the exact one.
nodes.descriptionZh: 先估一个大概值，再判断算得对不对。
evidence: Round numbers to the nearest 10 or 100 (or money amounts to the nearest dollar or pound) to estimate a sum or difference before calculating, e.g. $4.95 + $2.10 + $7.85 is about $15
Use addition to check a subtraction answer, or vice versa
Identify when a calculated answer, such as an amount of change, is unreasonable based on the estimate
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Before {{name}} works out a calculation, can they make a sensible rough guess — and then check their answer using the opposite operation?

nodes.descriptionEn: Split one whole into two equal parts and take one of them.
nodes.descriptionZh: 把一个整体平均分成两份，取其中一份。
evidence: Fold a shape into two equal parts and identify each as 'a half'
Find half of 8 objects by sharing into 2 equal groups
Identify whether a shape has been divided into halves or not (equal vs unequal parts)
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} is helping share a sandwich equally between two people, can they cut it so both pieces are the same size — and tell you each piece is called a half?

nodes.descriptionEn: The denominator says how many parts; the numerator says how many you take.
nodes.descriptionZh: 分母决定切几份，分子决定取几份。
evidence: Given a shape divided into 5 equal parts, identify one shaded part as 1/5
Explain that 3/4 means 3 parts each of size 1/4
Draw a model showing 2/6 as 2 pieces of a whole cut into 6
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If you cut a pizza into 6 equal slices, can {{name}} explain what 1/6 means — and then work out what 4/6 of the pizza looks like?

nodes.descriptionEn: The two numbers above and below the bar each mean something specific.
nodes.descriptionZh: 分数线上下两个数，各有各的含义。
evidence: Point to and name the numerator and denominator in any given fraction and explain what each tells you
Correctly classify fractions as unit, proper, improper, or mixed number with an example of each
Explain in own words why 2/4 and 1/2 are equivalent fractions
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} saw the fraction 3/4 written down, could they point to the numerator and the denominator — and explain what each number actually means?

nodes.descriptionEn: Put a fraction back on the number line and it regains its size.
nodes.descriptionZh: 把分数放回数轴，它才有大小。
evidence: Place 1/2, 1/4, 3/4 on a number line from 0 to 1
Identify that 1/3 lies between 0 and 1/2 on the number line
Understand that a fraction is a single number, not just 'part of a shape'
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If you draw a number line from 0 to 1, can {{name}} mark where 1/4, 1/2, and 3/4 should go — without any extra help?

nodes.descriptionEn: Different cuts, the same amount taken.
nodes.descriptionZh: 切法不同，占的份一样多。
evidence: Show that 1/2 = 2/4 using a diagram of equal parts
Use a fraction wall or bar model to find equivalent fractions
Explain why two fractions are equivalent by comparing the shaded areas
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} sees a bar divided into 4 equal parts with 2 shaded, can they tell you that's the same as 1/2 — and draw a different bar showing the same amount another way?

nodes.descriptionEn: The denominator stays put; only the numerators add.
nodes.descriptionZh: 分母不变，直接加分子。
evidence: Calculate 3/5 + 4/5 = 7/5 and explain it equals 1 2/5
Subtract 2/6 from 5/6
Solve addition problems where the sum exceeds the whole: 7/8 + 3/8
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If a recipe uses 5/8 of a bag of flour and then another 6/8, can {{name}} work out the total and explain what the answer means as a mixed number?

nodes.descriptionEn: Three notations for one number: fraction, decimal, percentage.
nodes.descriptionZh: 同一个数的三种写法：分数、小数、百分数。
evidence: Read and write decimal numbers correctly, identifying the value of each digit (ones, tenths, hundredths)
Use the % symbol correctly and explain that per cent means 'out of 100'
Convert between simple fractions, decimals, and percentages (e.g. 1/2 = 0.5 = 50%) and explain why they are equal
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} saw '0.5' and '50%' written down, could they explain that they both mean the same amount — and write them as a fraction too?

nodes.descriptionEn: When two ratios are equal, they form a proportion.
nodes.descriptionZh: 两个比相等，就构成比例。
evidence: Identify whether a real-world relationship is direct or inverse proportion and justify the choice
Set up and solve a direct-proportion equation (e.g. if 4 pens cost £6, find the cost of 10)
Sketch graphs showing direct proportion (straight line through origin) and inverse proportion (curve)
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Does {{name}} understand the difference between quantities that grow together at the same rate (direct proportion) and ones where one goes up as the other goes down — like more workers meaning fewer days to finish a job (inverse proportion)?

nodes.descriptionEn: Centimetres for a book, metres for a field — the wrong unit makes the number meaningless.
nodes.descriptionZh: 量书本用厘米，量操场用米——单位选错，数字就没意义。
evidence: Measure the length of a table in centimetres using a ruler
Weigh an object in grams using a scale
Measure the capacity of a container in millilitres using a measuring jug
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If you ask {{name}} whether to measure a swimming pool or a piece of paper in cm or m, can they pick the sensible unit for each — and explain why?

nodes.descriptionEn: Line up the zero mark with the start, hug the edge, and read.
nodes.descriptionZh: 把尺子的零刻度对准起点，贴着边读数。
evidence: Choose the most appropriate tool for measuring a given object

Align the zero mark of a ruler with the end of the object and read the measurement; for an offset or broken ruler, count the unit spaces or subtract the starting reading from the ending reading (e.g. 3 cm to 10 cm is 7 cm)

Measure lengths in inches, feet, centimetres, and metres using the correct tool. For example, use the centimetre marks on a metre stick to explain that 1 m is 100 cm, or mark off and check a line of a given length with a ruler.
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} needs to measure a piece of fabric about 80 cm long, can they pick the right tool — a short ruler or a tape measure — and use it accurately?

nodes.descriptionEn: How many unit squares tile the surface?
nodes.descriptionZh: 铺满一块地面需要多少个单位方块。
evidence: Count unit squares to find the area of an L-shaped figure
Measure the area of a book cover using square-centimetre tiles
Compare areas of two shapes by counting their unit squares
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} draws a shape on squared centimetre paper, can they find its area by counting the squares — including making a sensible estimate for any partial squares?

nodes.descriptionEn: Walk once around the shape — how far did you go?
nodes.descriptionZh: 绕着图形走一圈有多长。
evidence: Measure each side of a rectangle and add the lengths to find the perimeter
Calculate the perimeter of a regular shape given the side length
Explain that perimeter is the total distance around a shape
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} wants to put a decorative border around a rectangular picture frame 20 cm wide and 30 cm tall, can they work out the total length of border needed?

nodes.descriptionEn: Layer by layer, how many unit cubes fill it?
nodes.descriptionZh: 一层一层铺满，需要多少个单位小方块。
evidence: Use V = l × w × h to find the volume of a cuboid 4 cm × 3 cm × 5 cm = 60 cm³
Explain why packing a prism with unit cubes gives the same result as multiplying edge lengths
Compare the 60 cm³ cuboid with an irregular model built from 58 centimetre cubes, explaining that the formula works for the cuboid but the model's cubes must be counted
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} wants to work out how much soil fits in a plant box that is 40 cm long, 20 cm wide, and 15 cm deep, can they use a formula to calculate the volume?

nodes.descriptionEn: For one rectangle, area and perimeter are two different questions.
nodes.descriptionZh: 同一个长方形，面积和周长是两件不同的事。
evidence: Find the width of a room given area = 48 m² and length = 8 m
Calculate the area of a square with side 7.5 cm
Estimate the area of an irregular pond drawn on a cm² grid
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} wants to carpet a room 6.5 m × 4 m, can they calculate the area — and also work out how many metres of skirting board are needed around the edge?

nodes.nameZh: 三角形与平行四边形的面积
nodes.descriptionEn: Two identical triangles make one parallelogram.
nodes.descriptionZh: 两个一样的三角形拼成一个平行四边形。
evidence: Cut a right-angled triangle off one end of a parallelogram with base 8 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm, move it to the other end to make an 8 cm × 5 cm rectangle, and state the area as 40 cm²

Show that a right triangle with legs 6 cm and 4 cm is half of a 6 cm × 4 cm rectangle (12 cm²), and that an obtuse triangle with base 12 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm, drawn outside the triangle, is half of a parallelogram (42 cm²)

Decide that a formula gives the area of a parallelogram with base 10 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm (50 cm², not the 60 cm² from its slanted 6 cm side) but not of an irregular leaf shape, whose area must be estimated by counting squares
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} is cutting triangular pieces of cloth where the base is 8 cm and the height is 5 cm, can they use a formula to work out the area of each piece?

nodes.descriptionEn: Between metres and centimetres, what exactly is the factor?
nodes.descriptionZh: 米和厘米之间，到底是几倍的关系。
evidence: Convert 3.25 kg to 3250 g and 45 cm to 0.45 m, explaining why the count grows or shrinks; convert 5 g to 0.005 kg without adding or deleting zeros mechanically
Convert 2 hours 35 minutes to 155 minutes and 150 seconds to 2 minutes 30 seconds, preserving the mixed part or remainder and explaining why the rate is 60 rather than 100
Convert 8 weeks 3 days to 59 days and 2 years 3 months to 27 months; explain why an unspecified month cannot be converted to one fixed number of days
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Can {{name}} explain and show how to turn 3.25 kg into grams and 45 cm into metres, change 2 hours 35 minutes into minutes and 150 seconds into minutes and seconds, and make a small cm-to-mm conversion table? Ask how they chose each operation, kept any remainder, and why a month does not always have the same number of days.

nodes.descriptionEn: Sort shapes by the features of their edges and angles.
nodes.descriptionZh: 按边与角的特征，把图形分类。
evidence: Name a triangle, circle, rectangle, and square when shown them
Identify a shape correctly regardless of its size or orientation
Pick out all the triangles from a mixed set of shapes
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Can {{name}} point to shapes around the house — like a clock, a window, or a pizza — and correctly name whether each is a circle, triangle, rectangle, or square?

nodes.descriptionEn: Half a turn is 180 degrees; a full turn is 360.
nodes.descriptionZh: 转半圈是 180 度，转一整圈是 360 度。
evidence: Explain that a full turn is 360° and a right angle is 90°
Describe what 'one degree' means in terms of a fraction of a circle
State that an angle of 45° has turned through 45 one-degree angles
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} knows a full circle is 360 degrees, can they tell you how many degrees a quarter turn is — and explain roughly what one single degree looks like?

nodes.descriptionEn: Drag the three vertices and watch the three interior angles move.
nodes.descriptionZh: 拖动三个顶点，三个内角实时变化。
evidence: Find a missing angle in a triangle given two angles (using angle sum = 180°)
Calculate a missing angle in a quadrilateral (angle sum = 360°)
Calculate the interior angle of a regular hexagon from the angle sum formula
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} knows that angles in a triangle always add up to 180°, and two angles in a triangle are 55° and 70°, can they work out the third angle without measuring it?

nodes.nameEn: Angle Sums in Triangles and Polygons
nodes.nameZh: 三角形与多边形的内角和
nodes.descriptionEn: The interior angles always sum to 180 — and that can be proved.
nodes.descriptionZh: 内角和恒等于 180 度，这是可以证明的。
evidence: Calculate a missing angle in a triangle by subtracting the known angles from 180°
Find the sum of interior angles in a hexagon by dividing it into triangles
Calculate each interior and exterior angle of a regular polygon given the number of sides
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} knows two angles of a triangle are 50° and 70°, can they work out the third? And can they figure out the angles inside a regular pentagon?

nodes.descriptionEn: Never meeting is parallel; meeting at a right angle is perpendicular.
nodes.descriptionZh: 两条线永不相交，是平行；相交成直角，是垂直。
evidence: Point out horizontal and vertical lines in shapes and real-world contexts
Identify a pair of parallel lines (lines that never meet and are always the same distance apart)
Identify perpendicular lines (lines that meet at a right angle)
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} looks at a set of railway tracks or a window frame, can they point to which lines are parallel (never crossing) and which are perpendicular (meeting at a right angle)?

nodes.descriptionEn: Fold along this line and the two halves match exactly.
nodes.descriptionZh: 沿这条线折过去，两边完全重合。
evidence: Given half a butterfly shape and a mirror line, complete the other half on a grid
Complete a symmetric pattern on squared paper with a vertical line of symmetry
Check a completed figure by folding along the mirror line
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If you show {{name}} half a shape drawn on squared paper with a mirror line marked, can they draw the missing half so the whole shape is perfectly symmetrical?

nodes.descriptionEn: Cut a circle open and flatten it — it is almost a rectangle.
nodes.descriptionZh: 把圆剪开摊平，它几乎就是一个长方形。
evidence: Calculate the circumference and area of a circle given its radius or diameter
Find the perimeter or area of a composite shape made from rectangles and semicircles
Explain the relationship between π, diameter, and circumference informally
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} wants to know how far a bicycle wheel travels in one full rotation, can they use the diameter of the wheel and π (pi) to work out the circumference?

nodes.descriptionEn: The squares on the two legs add to the square on the hypotenuse.
nodes.descriptionZh: 两条直角边平方相加，等于斜边的平方。
evidence: Calculate the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle given the two shorter sides
Find a shorter side given the hypotenuse and the other short side
Use Pythagoras’ Theorem to find the distance between two points on a coordinate grid
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} wants to check whether a shelf bracket makes a perfect right angle and the sides measure 30 cm, 40 cm, and 50 cm, can they use Pythagoras to verify?

cnRef.chapter: 第十七章 勾股定理

nodes.descriptionEn: Symbols are shorthand for actions — read them correctly or compute wrongly.
nodes.descriptionZh: 符号是操作的速记，读懂它才能算得对。
evidence: Read 3 + 2 = 5 aloud as 'three plus two equals five'
Write a number sentence to match a concrete addition situation
Interpret the = sign as 'is the same as' rather than just 'the answer is'
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If you write '4 + 3 = 7' on paper, can {{name}} tell you what the plus sign, minus sign, and equals sign each mean?

nodes.descriptionEn: The same letter stands for a different number on each pan.
nodes.descriptionZh: 同一个字母在不同的盘子里代表不同的数。
evidence: In 7 + □ = 12, say that the box stands for a number we do not know yet
Look at several number sentences and pattern rules and say which symbols stand for numbers and which are operation or equals signs
Describe how a symbol is being used in a real situation (e.g. in 'n children each bring 2 apples', n can change from day to day, while in 4 + ? = 9 the ? is one unknown number)
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} sees a puzzle like 7 + □ = 12 on a homework sheet, can they explain that the box stands for a number we need to find?

nodes.descriptionEn: Translate a balance into an equation with a letter in it.
nodes.descriptionZh: 把「平衡」翻译成含字母的等式。
evidence: Write 'I think of a number, double it, and add 5 to get 17' as 2n + 5 = 17
Solve a one-step equation such as 3x = 24 and explain the reasoning
Express a word problem as an algebraic equation and find the unknown value
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} reads "I think of a number, double it, and add 5 to get 17," can they write that as an equation using a letter for the unknown and solve it?

nodes.descriptionEn: Doing the same thing to both pans keeps the balance true.
nodes.descriptionZh: 天平上两边同时做同一件事，等式依然成立。
evidence: Solve one-step and two-step linear equations in one variable
Solve equations requiring expansion of brackets and collection of like terms
Solve equations with the unknown on both sides and with fractional or negative coefficients
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} is given an equation like 3x + 7 = 22, can they work through the steps to find the value of x?

cnRef.chapter: 第三章 一元一次方程

nodes.descriptionEn: Gather the matching terms together and count them.
nodes.descriptionZh: 把相同的项并到一起，数一数有几个。
evidence: Identify like terms in an algebraic expression
Combine like terms involving positive and negative coefficients
Simplify expressions involving multiple variables and constant terms
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} sees an expression like "5a + 3b + 2a," can they simplify it by collecting the like terms to get "7a + 3b"?

cnRef.chapter: 第二章 整式的加减

nodes.descriptionEn: Multiply the bracket through — every term inside gets multiplied.
nodes.descriptionZh: 括号乘进去，每一项都要乘到。
evidence: Multiply a single positive term over a bracket to expand the expression
Multiply a negative term over a bracket, correctly handling signs
Combine expanding brackets with collecting like terms to simplify fully
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Can {{name}} expand a bracket like 3(2x + 5) by multiplying everything inside, to get 6x + 15?

cnRef.chapter: 第三章 一元一次方程

nodes.descriptionEn: Gather an expanded expression back into brackets.
nodes.descriptionZh: 把展开的式子重新收拢回括号。
evidence: Identify the highest common factor of all terms in an expression
Write the factorised form as a product of the HCF and a bracket
Check factorisation by expanding the brackets back out
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Can {{name}} look at an expression like "6x + 9" and rewrite it with the common factor taken out — as "3(2x + 3)"?

cnRef.chapter: 第十四章 整式的乘法与因式分解

nodes.descriptionEn: Two unknowns, two balances — solve them together.
nodes.descriptionZh: 两个未知数，两条平衡关系，联立求解。
evidence: Explain that the intersection of two lines represents values satisfying both equations
Find the approximate solution to a pair of simultaneous equations by reading a graph
Verify a proposed solution by substituting into both equations
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Can {{name}} explain that solving two equations simultaneously means finding the one pair of values that satisfies both at once — and show what that looks like on a graph?

cnRef.chapter: 第八章 二元一次方程组

nodes.descriptionEn: Two perpendicular number axes split the plane into four quadrants.
nodes.descriptionZh: 两条垂直的数轴，把平面分成四个象限。
evidence: Identify the x-axis, y-axis, and origin on a coordinate grid
Explain that (3, 5) means go 3 along the x-axis and 5 up the y-axis
Distinguish (2, 4) from (4, 2) by explaining each coordinate's meaning
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} looks at a map with a grid and you describe a location as "3 across and 5 up from the origin", can they find the exact point — and explain what each of the two numbers tells you?

cnRef.chapter: 第七章 平面直角坐标系

nodes.descriptionEn: Across first, then up — find the point from the origin.
nodes.descriptionZh: 先横后竖，从原点出发找到那个点。
evidence: Read the coordinates of a point on a grid as (3, 5)
Explain that the first number is the horizontal distance and the second is the vertical distance
Identify the coordinates of all vertices of a shape plotted on a grid
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} is playing a grid-based treasure map game, can they correctly say where the treasure is using two numbers — like "three across and four up" — from the corner?

nodes.nameEn: Plotting Points in the First Quadrant
nodes.descriptionEn: Pin each ordered pair to its spot on the grid.
nodes.descriptionZh: 把每一个有序数对钉在对应的位置。
evidence: Plot the point (4, 7) accurately on a first-quadrant grid
Graph a set of data pairs (e.g. time vs distance) as points on the coordinate plane
Read coordinates of a plotted point and explain what they represent in a given scenario
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If you tell {{name}} a car journey passes through grid points (2, 3), (5, 7), and (8, 4) on a map, can they plot those points and describe what the journey looks like?

nodes.descriptionEn: Slide, flip, turn — how the points of a shape move with it.
nodes.descriptionZh: 平移、翻转、旋转——图形上的点怎么跟着动。
evidence: Reflect a shape in a given mirror line (including diagonal lines) and state the coordinates of the image
Rotate a shape about a given centre by 90° or 180° and describe the result
Translate a shape by a given vector and verify that lengths and angles are preserved
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} is asked to rotate a triangle 90° clockwise around a fixed point, can they work out where each corner ends up — and confirm the triangle is still the same size and shape?

nodes.descriptionEn: A straight line — and its slope is the rate of change.
nodes.descriptionZh: 一条直线，斜率就是变化快慢。
evidence: Explain that changing m in y = mx + c alters the steepness and direction of the line
Identify the y-intercept of a line from its equation and from its graph
Determine whether a given equation will produce a straight line or a curve
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} sees the equation y = 2x + 3, can they explain what the graph will look like — including how steep it is and where it crosses the y-axis?

nodes.descriptionEn: Which way it opens, where the vertex sits, how it changes.
nodes.descriptionZh: 开口方向、顶点位置、变化的两端。
evidence: Explain why x² produces a U-shaped curve rather than a straight line
Plot a simple quadratic such as y = x² − 4 from a table of values
Read approximate solutions from a quadratic graph (e.g., where y = 0)
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Can {{name}} recognise that an equation like y = x² produces a curved graph rather than a straight line, and use a plotted curve to estimate values?

nodes.descriptionEn: The trend hidden inside a cloud of points.
nodes.descriptionZh: 一团点里藏着的走向。
evidence: Plot 10 data points on a scatter graph with correct axis labels and a consistent scale
Draw a line of best fit by eye, ensuring roughly equal numbers of points above and below
Use the line of best fit to estimate a y-value for a given x-value within the data range
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} has data comparing hours of sleep and test scores for 10 students, can they plot the points on a scatter graph, draw a line of best fit, and use it to predict a score for someone who slept 7 hours?

nodes.descriptionEn: The closer the points hug a line, the stronger the correlation.
nodes.descriptionZh: 点越贴近一条直线，相关越强。
evidence: Plot bivariate data on a scatter graph and describe the type of correlation observed
Draw a line of best fit by eye and use it to estimate a value within the data range
Explain what positive, negative, and no correlation mean in the context of real data (e.g., temperature vs. ice-cream sales)
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} plotted a scatter graph — say, comparing hours of revision and test scores — could they draw a line of best fit, describe the pattern, and use it to make a prediction?

nodes.descriptionEn: Sort the mess into piles before you can read anything from it.
nodes.descriptionZh: 杂乱的数据先分堆，才谈得上观察。
evidence: Sort a set of shapes by colour and count how many in each group
Sort objects by size (big/small) and state how many in each category
Identify which category has the most/fewest after sorting and counting
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Can {{name}} sort a pile of objects — like buttons, coins, or toy animals — into groups and count how many are in each group?

nodes.descriptionEn: Count with symbols, then lay it all out in a table.
nodes.descriptionZh: 用符号计数，用表格归位。
evidence: Read a pictogram where each symbol represents one item
Construct a tally chart from collected data
Draw a block diagram, or build a concrete graph with one real object per data value, and give it a title, category labels and the data source (e.g. 'Our class survey, Monday')
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Can {{name}} read a simple chart or pictogram — like one showing how many children chose each favourite fruit — and answer questions like "which was most popular"?

nodes.descriptionEn: The value that shows up most often.
nodes.descriptionZh: 出现次数最多的那个数。
evidence: Point to the mode on a pictograph or bar graph of favourite fruits and on a line plot of shoe sizes, and say it is the most common response
Name every mode when two or more categories tie for the most (e.g. apples, bananas and grapes each chosen 6 times), and say there is no mode when every value occurs exactly once
Find the modes of two classes' favourite-fruit tallies and say whether the modes are the same, even when the counts in each category are different
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: After a family vote on pizza toppings, can {{name}} tell you which topping was chosen most often (the mode) and what it means if several toppings tie?

nodes.descriptionEn: Total divided by count — but the mean gets dragged by outliers.
nodes.descriptionZh: 总数除以份数——但平均数会被极端值拽走。
evidence: Calculate the mean of five test scores: 72, 85, 90, 68, 95
Explain what the mean represents and how it differs from individual data values
Find a missing data value given the mean and all other values
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If the family scored 6, 8, 7, 5, and 9 on a board game over five rounds, can {{name}} work out the mean (average) score?

nodes.descriptionEn: The value in the middle — untouched by outliers.
nodes.descriptionZh: 排在正中间的那个数，不受极端值影响。
evidence: Put five values such as 12, 7, 15, 9 and 10 in order and state that the median is 10, the middle value
Find the median of an even number of values such as 4, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12 by finding the value halfway between the two middle values 7 and 8 (7.5, or 7½)
Find the median of a data set with repeated values, such as 1, 2, 2, 2, 9 (median 2), and explain that at least half of the values are at or below 2 and at least half are at or above 2
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If {{name}} lines up the number of pages five friends read, can they find the middle number — and work out the median for six friends, even when it falls halfway between two numbers?

nodes.descriptionEn: From 'impossible' to 'certain', with the possible in between.
nodes.descriptionZh: 从「绝不可能」到「必然发生」，中间是可能。
evidence: Place everyday events on a 0-to-1 probability scale with justification
Explain why a fair six-sided die gives each number a probability of 1/6
Distinguish between equally likely outcomes (fair coin) and unequally likely outcomes (biased spinner)
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Can {{name}} explain that probability goes from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain), place events on that scale as numbers, and tell you whether a game is fair or not?

nodes.nameZh: 所有可能结果的概率之和为一
nodes.descriptionEn: Add up the likelihood of every outcome and you get exactly one.
nodes.descriptionZh: 每一种结果的可能性加起来，正好是一。
evidence: List all outcomes of spinning a 4-colour spinner and verify their probabilities add up to 1
Calculate P(not rolling a 3) as 1 − 1/6 = 5/6 using the complement rule
Spot an error in a probability table where the values don't sum to 1 and explain what's wrong
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: If the probability of it raining tomorrow is 0.3, can {{name}} work out the probability of it NOT raining — and explain why all probabilities in a situation must add up to 1?

nodes.descriptionEn: Decide the question first; only then decide how to gather the data.
nodes.descriptionZh: 先想清楚要回答什么问题，再决定怎么收集数据。
evidence: Pose an investigation question such as 'Do Year 5 students sleep less on school nights?', refining a vague question (e.g. 'Do kids like sport?') into one that data can answer, and plan how to collect the data
Choose and justify a display (column graph, dot plot or table) for the collected data
Write a short report that answers the question and states one limitation of the data
nodes.assessmentPromptEn: Could {{name}} come up with their own question — like whether kids sleep less on school nights — plan how to collect the data, and report what they found?
